ai.description: This 8–10 cm skink is bronze-brown with a dark lateral stripe. It features fused, transparent eyelids forming a spectacle and smooth, overlapping scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Asian Snake-eyed Skink is best identified by its lack of movable eyelids, which creates a permanent, spectacle-like covering over the eyes, unlike other Indian skinks.
ai.habitat: The Asian Snake-eyed Skink inhabits dry, open deciduous forests and scrublands, often found under leaf litter or stones at elevations ranging from sea level to 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Asian Snake-eyed Skink is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small invertebrates among leaf litter and rocky crevices during the warmest parts of the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ablepharus pannonicus* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ablepharus pannonicus* occurs in the arid regions of northwestern India (Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab) and Pakistan, typically inhabiting elevations from sea level to 1,500m.
